optimization: Snapshot serialization: emit the per-directory and per-entry fixed wire records as one packed memcpy instead of one bounds-checked call per field (~400,000 memcpy calls instead of ~3,200,000 at 200,000 entries).
method: Interleaved randomized A/B in one session, 5 processes per arm, 5 warm-up + 5 measured repetitions, release-test preset, identical product SHA in both arms.
noise_spread: Both arms show 16-24% spread across run medians. The apparent 11.9% candidate regression is inside the union of both arms' spreads, and the candidate's own spread is the tighter of the two. Machine load during this session was high and non-stationary (multiple long-running node/IDE processes saturated the CPU), so the direction of this delta is not trustworthy.
correctness_checks: The change was verified byte-exact before measurement: a new test pinned the packed-record layout against a hand-emitted reference buffer, SerializedSnapshotSize against the emitted byte count, negative int64 volume ids, all seven id pairs, timestamps, and the size/allocation trio. ffprotocol_tests passed with zero failures before reversion. This was a correctness-quality change, not a quantity-of-work reduction in the measured path.
memory_impact: None: the writer already wrote directly into caller-owned storage; packing the record removed call overhead, not allocations.
reason: The measured delta is smaller than the observed natural variation, so per section 1 (measure before modifying) and section 13 (statistical discipline) it cannot be claimed as a win. It also does not attack the dominant cost: profiling showed the first-generation path is dominated by per-entry std::wstring heap allocation and pointer chasing over the 200,000-entry projection, not by serialization call count. Under non-stationary host load the measurement cannot resolve a <1 ms effect. Reverted to keep the tree honest; retained as evidence that serialization call overhead is not the bottleneck.
note: Two real non-blocking defects were found and repaired in the same file while investigating and are retained: a dead uint32_t-vs-size_t comparison in Reader::ReadWString that static analysis flagged as always-false.
